nodes.name: Capture Webhook
nodes.notes: POST only, and the path is the workflow id spelled out rather than left to the node id n8n mints, so the production URL is one a client can be configured with before this file has ever reached an instance. Response mode onReceived, so the request is answered as it lands and the pass runs behind it: the alternative holds the socket open through extraction, the findings write and the invocation of ar-score, none of which a capture client asked about. authentication is written none rather than left off, because a default nobody wrote down is a decision nobody reviewed; what stands in front of this path is whatever fronts the instance, and this canvas judges shape rather than caller. typeVersion 2 is what the other nodes here are held to as well: nothing in this repository validates an n8n parameter name or version, no n8n package being installed, so these four are reviewed rather than checked.

parameters.query:
WITH envelope AS (
  SELECT nullif($1::jsonb, 'null'::jsonb) AS posted
),
claim AS (
  SELECT
    CASE
      WHEN e.posted ->> 'sourceId' ~ '^[0-9]{1,18}$'
      THEN (e.posted ->> 'sourceId')::bigint
    END AS source_id
  FROM envelope e
),
source AS (
  SELECT
    s.id,
    s.domain_id,
    s.kind,
    s.endpoint,
    s.parser_config,
    s.contract,
    s.consecutive_failures,
    s.last_success_at,
    s.last_failure_at,
    s.enabled,
    s.flagged
  FROM sources s
  WHERE s.id = (SELECT source_id FROM claim)
)
-- The first node after the trigger, and the shape the parent design fixes for every
-- workflow in this set (.specs/2026-08-19-research-pipeline-port.md, section 4): the
-- domain's personas and taxonomy, read as ONE query answering exactly one row. Both
-- halves are argued in full on ar-ingest's Load Domain Context, which asks the same
-- question of the same tables and is not repeated here. What is written out below is
-- the half that differs, which is how this canvas gets a domain at all.

-- Nothing has named one. ar-ingest is invoked with a run id and reads its domain back
-- off that row, an id the dispatcher wrote. All this trigger carries is a POST body
-- from a stranger, and no part of it has been judged: capture-contract.ts runs two
-- node groups below, after the raw body has been stored. So the domain is resolved
-- through the source the envelope CLAIMS, and this statement is where the claim is
-- read.

-- The whole posted body binds as ONE jsonb parameter rather than one parameter per
-- member. A body may be a bare string, a number or a list as readily as an object,
-- JSON.stringify makes every one of those a valid jsonb literal, and the members are
-- then read where a comment can say what each one is instead of inside an expression
-- no gate reads. The nullif is the other half of that: JSON.stringify(null) binds the
-- JSON null literal rather than SQL NULL, so a request with no body at all would
-- otherwise arrive here as a value.

-- ->> answers NULL for every jsonb that is not an object, measured on this schema for
-- a string, a number, a list and the null literal, so a body that is not an object
-- needs no guard in front of the read: the pattern test is handed NULL, the CASE
-- answers NULL, and nothing raises over a shape somebody else chose.

-- The digit bound is {1,18} rather than +, and the difference between them is a
-- raise. A longer run of digits matches + and then overflows the bigint cast, which
-- is an error this node could not survive; eighteen digits sits inside bigint's
-- nineteen, and no sources id is going to reach it.

-- Three readings come out of this row and they are not two. A null source_id means
-- the envelope named no source this statement could read. A source_id with a null
-- domain_id means it named one that matches no sources row. A domain_id means the
-- capture resolved, and an empty list beside it is a domain that states no personas,
-- no categories, no terms or no criteria. Read them in that order: a length says
-- nothing until both ids have been read.

-- Nothing here refuses, which is the rule capture-contract.ts states from the other
-- side. The raw body is stored before anything judges it, so a node turning an
-- unreadable source id away HERE would lose the capture at exactly the point that
-- ordering exists to protect. What this answers instead is a row saying what it could
-- and could not resolve. One thing the group below cannot do with it is store a
-- document under a null domain: documents.domain_id is NOT NULL, so a capture naming
-- a source this database does not hold has no row to be written to, and what that
-- pass records is that group's to decide.

-- The source row is fetched here rather than by a lookup node below because this is
-- where it is read anyway: the domain is reached THROUGH it, so the round trip is
-- already spent and a second node would be a second branch to reason about. to_jsonb
-- over the CTE is what projects it, so the member list is declared once, in the CTE
-- above, and a column added there travels with no second edit. This node acts on none
-- of them: enabled and flagged are answers rather than decisions here.

-- The posted body is not echoed forward. This node's answer REPLACES the item the
-- trigger was handed, which is what run_id travels for on ar-ingest's twin, but a
-- capture body IS the payload and copying it onto every item below would carry the
-- whole capture through the pass. The node that stores it reads it back off
-- $('Capture Webhook').first().json.body, which is the handle every node here has on
-- the request.

-- Every list is ordered, which nothing downstream requires and every reader benefits
-- from: two captures against one unchanged domain hand the nodes below the same lists
-- in the same order, so a diff between two passes is about the captures rather than
-- about the order a planner happened to return rows in.
SELECT
  (SELECT source_id FROM claim) AS source_id,
  (SELECT domain_id FROM source) AS domain_id,

  -- The source row, cut to the members the groups below read. It is also the
  -- resolution path: domain_id comes off it, so every list beneath is scoped by a
  -- column of this row rather than by anything the envelope said. parser_config and
  -- contract are what the extraction reads, the two stamps and the counter are what
  -- source-health.ts turns into a verdict, and kind and endpoint travel because a
  -- reader holding one of these rows should not have to go and fetch what it is.
  (SELECT to_jsonb(s) FROM source s) AS source,

  -- The domain row, cut to the members the nodes below read. feature_version is the
  -- one that has to travel: a document written on this path is read against the same
  -- pin ar-ingest writes, and fetching one integer separately is the lookup node this
  -- shape exists to avoid. NULL rather than an empty object when nothing resolved,
  -- which is the same discriminator domain_id carries.
  (SELECT jsonb_build_object(
     'id', d.id,
     'slug', d.slug,
     'name', d.name,
     'settings', d.settings,
     'feature_version', d.feature_version,
     'embedding_model', d.embedding_model)
     FROM domains d
    WHERE d.id = (SELECT domain_id FROM source)) AS domain,

  -- The personas. system_text is operator-owned prose and is the trusted half of what
  -- prompt-frame.ts composes around an untrusted chunk. No node on this canvas makes
  -- a model call, so nothing here reads them today; they are selected because the
  -- design fixes personas and taxonomy as what this node fetches, and because a
  -- capture that grows a judging step should not grow a second lookup with it.
  COALESCE(
    (SELECT jsonb_agg(jsonb_build_object(
       'id', p.id,
       'role', p.role,
       'system_text', p.system_text)
       ORDER BY p.role, p.id)
       FROM personas p
      WHERE p.domain_id = (SELECT domain_id FROM source)),
    '[]'::jsonb) AS personas,

  -- The categories, which are the buckets the terms below are filed under. key rather
  -- than id is what a reader downstream matches on: features.ts builds a column name
  -- out of it and static-gate.ts groups hits by it, so the surrogate id travels for
  -- an operator's benefit and the key is what the libraries read.
  COALESCE(
    (SELECT jsonb_agg(jsonb_build_object(
       'id', c.id,
       'key', c.key,
       'name', c.name,
       'parent_id', c.parent_id)
       ORDER BY c.key, c.id)
       FROM categories c
      WHERE c.domain_id = (SELECT domain_id FROM source)),
    '[]'::jsonb) AS categories,

  -- The terms, joined to their category's key rather than carrying category_id. Four
  -- members and this exact spelling, because three libraries read this one list and
  -- each reads a different subset of it: static-gate.ts takes pattern, weight and
  -- polarity, features.ts takes pattern and category, and feature-version.ts takes
  -- all four. A term list selected without the join satisfies the first reader and
  -- starves the other two, with nothing failing.
  COALESCE(
    (SELECT jsonb_agg(jsonb_build_object(
       'category', c.key,
       'pattern', t.pattern,
       'weight', t.weight,
       'polarity', t.polarity)
       ORDER BY c.key, t.pattern, t.id)
       FROM terms t
       JOIN categories c ON c.id = t.category_id
      WHERE c.domain_id = (SELECT domain_id FROM source)),
    '[]'::jsonb) AS terms,

  -- The criteria, joined to their category the same way. Nothing on this canvas reads
  -- them: they are ar-score's subject, and the group that closes this pass hands that
  -- workflow the findings to score rather than this context, so it fetches its own.
  -- They are selected here because the taxonomy is these three tables, and a node
  -- group added below reads them without a second lookup.
  COALESCE(
    (SELECT jsonb_agg(jsonb_build_object(
       'id', k.id,
       'category', c.key,
       'value', k.value,
       'kind', k.kind)
       ORDER BY c.key, k.kind, k.id)
       FROM criteria k
       JOIN categories c ON c.id = k.category_id
      WHERE k.domain_id = (SELECT domain_id FROM source)),
    '[]'::jsonb) AS criteria

parameters.content:
## Posted, Not Scheduled

This workflow starts when something outside this system POSTs to it, and the Webhook node on this canvas is the whole of what makes that possible. It holds no clock and may not acquire one: `ar-dispatch` carries the only Schedule Trigger in the system, and `tests/invariants/workflows.test.ts` counts them across every built workflow and names the one file allowed to hold one.

It is also the first workflow here that ARMS. `ar-ingest` is reached through an Execute Workflow node, and activating a workflow whose only trigger is that one registers nothing at all; a webhook registers a URL. `scripts/activate-workflows.sh` reads that split off each built artifact rather than off a list kept beside it, which is what lets this file change its answer without an edit anywhere else.

### What arrives, and what has judged it

One item per request, carrying `headers`, `params`, `query` and `body` among others. `body` is the capture envelope, and NOTHING has looked at it: `capture-contract.ts` runs below, after the raw body has been stored, which is the ordering that makes a refused capture a stored failure instead of a lost one. So the first node to read anything off the envelope is `Load Domain Context`, and all it reads is the source the envelope claims.

That read happens in SQL rather than in the expression beside it. The whole body binds as one jsonb parameter, the source id is taken out of it under a bounded digit pattern, and both the pattern and what it refuses are commented at the statement. An expression can import nothing and is read by no gate here, so a rule with any shape to it belongs where a comment can explain it.

### The boundary is the contract, not the caller

What this canvas judges is SHAPE: the envelope against `capture-contract.ts`, and the claimed source id against the `sources` table. Neither of those asks WHO posted, and the Webhook node declares `authentication` as `none`. Arming this workflow therefore publishes a path that writes rows, and whatever fronts the instance is the whole of what stands between that path and anybody who can reach it. `docs/architecture/04-sources.md` is where the contract a client writes to is documented.
